state.goal: Independently calculate the exact topological discriminating power of one binary rounded-qames feature on five named traditions, conditional on one innovation/no loss; do not infer actual genealogy.
inputs: Existing phyla-waves-assessment.json PW-C1 reports Tiberian/Babylonian rounded versus Secunda/Jerome/Palestinian unrounded, with source/chronology caveats.
Existing reading-tradition-edge-assessment.json distinguishes observed similarity from independently established genealogy.
Counting family: fully resolved rooted non-plane binary trees, five distinct labelled leaves, unlabelled internal nodes, no branch lengths or chronology.
Conditional model: known ancestral state0; Tiberian/Babylonian state1 and other three state0; exactly one0-to1 gain, no loss/contact/parallel origin.
constraints: Jev selects operational method, not the mathematical answer or historical truth.
Retain every compatible topology; do not elect a unique tree, treat family fractions as probabilities or apply the character to uncertain evidence as if certain.
No broad source recovery or duplicated methodology summary; preserve input bytes and source roles.
No central model/task changes, persistent service or dependency installation.

verification_route.instructions: Choose an independently checkable finite mathematical route.

criteria.two_enumerators_state_assignment_and_bij: Enumerate all five-leaf trees via canonical root bipartitions; independently enumerate them by fixed-label insertion; compare complete sets. Independently solve binary internal-state assignments for one gain/no loss, compare to the clade predicate, and prove the clade-collapse count by bijection.
criteria.planar_quotient_and_clade_collapse: Count fully labelled plane trees via Catalan numbers, prove the free left/right quotient, and independently enumerate the clade-collapsed four-leaf family; retain its full expansions and verify all assumptions.
